inputs.sbc_source: SEC XBRL companyfacts (CIK 4127), TTM to 2026-07-03: ShareBasedCompensation cash-flow add-back 232.4 + PaymentsRelatedToTaxWithholdingForShareBasedCompensation 42.6, summed because Skyworks publishes no combined SBC-incl-withholding figure in its non-GAAP reconciliation
inputs.share_count_basis: Weighted-average diluted shares for the quarter ended 2026-07-03 (10-Q Q3 FY2026), 151.4M. Held FLAT: SBC is fully expensed in the flows. The ~89M new shares to be issued to Qorvo holders at close (0.960 x ~93M Qorvo shares) are deliberately EXCLUDED -- this is a standalone valuation of pre-close Skyworks; see valuation_philosophy.
inputs.fiscal_year_end: 52/53-week year ending the Friday closest to 30 September (FY2025 ended 2025-10-03; FY2026 ends 2026-10-02)
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-10-01T20:00:01Z regular close (Yahoo regularMarketTime; no 2026-10-02 bar yet at valuation time)
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows, USD WACC. Risk-free 4.25% (10y UST), equity beta ~1.2 (RF semis, Apple-concentrated), ERP 5.0% -> cost of equity ~10.25%. Debt is $497M against ~$12.6B market cap (~4% weight) at ~5% pre-tax -> WACC ~10.0%, used in ALL three scenarios. Risk is charged once: Apple concentration and the smartphone cycle live in the scenario flows and the 25% bear weight, not in a WACC premium or per-scenario WACC differences.
inputs.lease_treatment: Operating leases are small (facility leases, <2% of revenue) and are inside the GAAP operating costs that the EBITDA margin is built from; lease liabilities NOT added to net debt. One treatment, applied once.
inputs.nci_treatment: None -- wholly-owned subsidiaries, no non-controlling interest.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF component DCF (routing table row 'operating company, cyclical'), mid-cycle normalised. Skyworks is a US RF front-end semiconductor maker -- not a bank/REIT/holdco -- so the owner-FCF engine applies. The 'live takeover' row of the routing table does not apply because Skyworks is the ACQUIRER of Qorvo, not a target receiving fixed consideration; per the task brief SWKS is valued STANDALONE, with the merger flagged in valuation_philosophy. FY0 = FY2026E: revenue 3,949 = 9M FY26 actual 2,913.9 (10-Q, quarter ended 2026-07-03) + Q4 FY26 guidance midpoint ~1,035 ($1.01-1.06B). FY2026 closes today (2026-10-02) so year 1 of the projection is FY2027. last_fcf is OWNER FCF on the trailing twelve months to 2026-07-03: OCF 716.2 (1,300.8 - 1,100.8 + 516.2) - capex 282.0 = reported FCF 434.2, less SBC 232.4 and equity-award withholding 42.6 = 159.2 (4.0% of revenue). That TTM figure is a TROUGH: 9M FY26 OCF fell to 516 from 1,101 on Qorvo transaction costs, a working-capital build and capex stepped up to ~7% of revenue for Broad Markets capacity; it is not carried forward. The projection is built from components (adj. EBITDA pre-SBC -> SBC -> depreciation -> 20% cash tax -> capex -> working capital) at mid-cycle levels: FY20-25 owner-FCF margins were 18.6/17.4/11.9/29.9/34.7/20.3% (FY23-24 flattered by inventory release and sub-4% capex). Adj. EBITDA (pre-SBC, ex merger/restructuring) ran ~29% in FY25 and ~27-28% in Q3-Q4 FY26 (non-GAAP op income $182M on $935M + ~$74M depreciation). D&A path is DEPRECIATION ONLY (7.2% of TTM revenue); acquired-intangible amortization ($175M TTM, mostly the 2021 Silicon Labs I&A purchase) is excluded so it gives no tax shield -- conservative. Cash tax 20%: FY25 cash taxes paid $147.1M on ~$684M of SBC-and-depreciation-burdened EBIT = 21.5%; FY24 and FY23 similar. Interest income: other non-operating income ~$47M TTM is not deducted from last_fcf because net cash is only $317M (below the 1x-FCF-base materiality rule on a mid-cycle base) and the projection is unlevered from EBITDA, so neither interest income nor the ~$26M interest expense enters the projected flows. Net cash = cash 790.0 + marketable securities 9.2 current + 14.6 non-current - 496.9 senior notes at 2026-07-03 (the $500M notes current at 2026-04-03 were repaid in Q3 FY26). Q4 FY26 dividends (~$107M) and any pre-close merger spending will lower it. Buybacks: FY2025 $830.2M, TTM only $7.5M -- repurchases were effectively suspended under the merger agreement, so the flat count is a modelling convention the company is not currently funding; the FY2025 pace shows it historically was a funded repurchaser. Dividend $0.71/qtr (~$430M/yr) is a distribution of owner FCF, not a deduction from it.

historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR (3yr 1.7%, 5yr 6.7%) diverges by far more than 30% from revenue (3yr -9.3%) and GAAP EPS (3yr -26.7%, 5yr -8.6%). Book value has held up because FY22-25 earnings were retained net of dividends/buybacks while revenue fell ~25% from the FY2022 peak of $5.49B; EPS fell further on amortization, merger and restructuring charges and operating deleverage. All CAGRs end at FY2025 and straddle a cycle peak (FY2021-22), so none is a forward growth rate. The 3yr equity figure is selected as the conservative anchor; the base revenue path compounds at ~2.3%/yr over FY27-36.
historical_growth.notes: FCF CAGRs are on the OWNER-FCF series (reported FCF - SBC - equity-award withholding): FY20 625.4, FY21 887.1, FY22 651.5, FY23 1,425.1, FY24 1,451.1, FY25 829.0. Owner-FCF 3yr CAGR (8.4%) exceeds reported (5.7%) only because FY22 was a heavy-capex year (8.9% of revenue); SBC itself has risen from 3.6% of revenue (FY22) to 5.7% (FY25) and 5.8% TTM -- an increasing share of the cost base is being paid in stock. The FY22 -> FY25 endpoints are peak-to-trough on revenue, so the FCF CAGRs mostly measure working-capital and capex timing, not growth.

base.narrative: Apple's iPhone dual-sourcing takes ~20% of Skyworks' Apple content as the new generation ramps, cutting FY27 revenue ~5% (Apple ~57% of revenue x ~20% loss, partly offset by Broad Markets +10%); Broad Markets then carries growth back to 4%/yr, decelerating to 3%.
base.growth_rationale: FY27 -5%: Mobile -11 to -12pp from the content loss, Broad Markets (~42% of revenue) +10-12% on Wi-Fi 7 / data centre / automotive demand running ahead of supply. FY28-31 3.5-4% as Broad Markets compounds against a flat smartphone unit market; 3% thereafter.
base.ebitda_margin_rationale: 28% in FY27 = trough-level fab under-absorption from the lost Apple volume (Q3 FY26 ran ~27.4%, Q4 FY26 guide ~28%); recovers to 31.5% mid-cycle as Broad Markets mix (higher gross margin) rises -- below the FY23 ~40% peak and the FY22 level, which assumed the old Apple share.
base.capex_rationale: 7% in FY27 (FY26 is running ~7% for Broad Markets capacity), settling at 6% = the FY20-25 average of ~6.5% excluding the FY21 12.5% outlier; D&A converges to capex at 6%.

bull.narrative: The Apple content loss proves smaller and one-generation only (Skyworks retains the main PA/FEM sockets), Broad Markets growth engines grow mid-teens as supply catches up with demand, and 5G-Advanced / Wi-Fi 7 content per device lifts Mobile dollar content in a flat unit market. Margins return toward the mid-30s on mix and utilisation.

bear.narrative: Dual-sourcing is the start of structural erosion at Apple, not a one-off: the full 25% content loss lands in FY27 and a further socket is lost the next generation, while Chinese RF entrants and Qualcomm's modem-RF integration pressure Android share and pricing. Broad Markets growth only offsets the decline from FY29, SBC stays sticky in dollars (rising as a % of a shrinking base) and fab under-absorption holds adj. EBITDA in the mid-20s.

scenario_narratives.base: Mid-cycle standalone Skyworks. Apple's dual-sourcing of a premier RF socket costs ~20% of Apple content as the new iPhone generation ramps, so FY27 revenue falls ~5% to ~$3.75B before Broad Markets (Wi-Fi 7, data centre, automotive, defence -- growing ~10-15% with demand ahead of supply) brings consolidated growth back to 3-4%. Adj. EBITDA (pre-SBC) troughs at 28% and recovers to 31.5% -- well below the FY22-23 peak because the old Apple share is not coming back. Capex normalises from ~7% to 6%. Owner-FCF margin ~14% in FY27 rising to ~16%, i.e. below the FY20-25 average of ~22% which was flattered by FY23-24 inventory releases and sub-4% capex.
scenario_narratives.bull: The content loss is shallow and temporary, Broad Markets becomes the majority of revenue faster than expected, and rising RF complexity (5G-Advanced, Wi-Fi 7, satellite-to-phone) lifts dollar content per handset. Revenue flat in FY27 then 5-7% growth; adj. EBITDA back to 35% on mix and fab utilisation; capex 5.5%. Still a standalone case -- no Qorvo synergies are credited.
scenario_narratives.bear: Apple diversification is structural: a full 25% content loss in FY27 (-12% revenue) and further share loss the next generation (-3%), with Chinese suppliers and Qualcomm's integrated modem-RF squeezing the Android book. Broad Markets only offsets the decline from FY29. Adj. EBITDA stuck at 25-27%, SBC sticky at ~6% of a smaller revenue base, capex 6.5% to defend filter technology. Owner-FCF margin ~11-13%.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% house default to 25% because ~57% of revenue still depends on a single customer that has just demonstrated it will dual-source and re-bid sockets each generation -- the single-customer-dependency trigger in the method. Base 50% because the Q3 FY26 print and Q4 guide show Broad Markets growth and Mobile holding up better than the February 2026 selloff implied. Bull cut from 35% to 25% because it needs two independent things to go right (a shallow, temporary Apple loss AND sustained double-digit Broad Markets growth) and gets no credit for Qorvo synergies on this standalone basis.

valuation_philosophy.summary: STANDALONE, PRE-CLOSE VALUATION WITH LIMITED FORWARD RELEVANCE. (1) The Skyworks-Qorvo merger (announced 2025-10-27; both shareholder votes passed 2026-02-11; all regulatory clearances obtained by 2026-09-30) is expected to close on or about 2026-10-05 -- three days after this valuation date. Closing risk is now minimal. (2) At close Qorvo holders receive 0.960 Skyworks shares + $32.50 cash per Qorvo share (~89M new SWKS shares and ~$3B of cash consideration, largely debt-funded), leaving Skyworks holders with ~63% of the combined company. From that point a SWKS share is a ~63/37 claim on a ~$7.7B-revenue, ~$2.1B-adjusted-EBITDA combined RF/analog company with $500M+ of targeted cost synergies and new acquisition debt -- NOT the standalone Skyworks valued here. This model excludes the new shares, the new debt, Qorvo's cash flows and the synergies, so it answers 'what is standalone Skyworks worth?', which stops being the security's economics within days. It should be superseded by a combined-company valuation once the first post-close 10-Q gives a pro forma balance sheet and share count. (3) The standalone business has shrunk: revenue fell from a $5.49B FY2022 peak to $4.09B in FY2025 and a ~$3.95B FY2026 run-rate (quarters of $935M-$1.04B), first on the post-pandemic smartphone slowdown and then on Apple's February 2026 decision to dual-source a premier RF socket for iPhone 17 (~20-25% content loss). Because of that cyclicality and the Apple concentration the projection is built at MID-CYCLE margins from components, not from the trough TTM owner FCF ($159M, 4% of revenue, depressed by merger costs, a working-capital build and capacity capex) nor from the FY23-24 peak (~30-35%, flattered by inventory release). The gap between this standalone value and the market price is best read as the market's valuation of the merger (synergies and Qorvo's diversification away from Apple) plus SBC treatment -- not as a standalone mispricing. (4) Result: the house (SBC-expensed) weighted value sits well below the market price and the price also sits ABOVE the street (SBC-as-non-cash) weighted value -- band_position above 100% -- so not even the most generous accounting regime justifies the price on standalone flows. Every scenario's terminal value binds on the cyclical exit cap (12x base, 14x bull, 10x bear owner FCF), below today's ~15x EV / FY2025 owner FCF, so no multiple expansion is assumed. The price is pricing the combination; on standalone numbers the stock does not meet the 15% hurdle in any scenario.
key_risks_to_valuation: Merger close (~2026-10-05) changes the share count (+~89M), the balance sheet (~$3B cash consideration, debt-funded) and the cash flows; this standalone value has little forward relevance beyond the close
Apple concentration (~57% of revenue): depth and persistence of the iPhone dual-sourcing content loss is the dominant swing factor between scenarios
Smartphone unit cycle and RF share competition from Qualcomm (modem-RF integration), Broadcom (FBAR filters) and Chinese entrants
Mid-cycle margin assumption: adj. EBITDA has run ~27-29% in FY25-26 versus ~40% at the FY23 level; the base assumes partial recovery to 31.5%
US-China export controls, Entity List restrictions and tariffs on Asia-billed revenue
SBC has risen to ~5.8% of revenue; the house basis expenses it in full, and the street basis memo shows how much of the price rests on treating it as non-cash
